meta.title: Check your understanding: Efficiency over time

objectives: Explain what a certified record efficiency is and how it is measured
Compare one-sun, tandem and concentrator records with the single-junction limit
Explain why record cells are more efficient than the modules that go on roofs

questions.prompt: The dashed III-V multi-junction line sits far above the others on the chart. Why is it not a fair comparison with the one-sun lines?
choices: It has not been certified by an independent lab
Its cells are much larger than the others
It is measured under sunlight concentrated hundreds of times
It counts the heat the cell gives off as well as the electricity
questions.explain: Concentrating sunlight hundreds of times raises the efficiency limits for any cell, so the page draws that line dashed and apart from the cells measured at one sun (1000 W/m²). Every record on the chart, including this one, counts only once an independent lab has certified it.

questions.prompt: The Shockley–Queisser limit is about 33 % in standard sunlight, yet silicon's own ceiling is about 29.4 %. Why is silicon's lower?
choices: Its 1.12 eV gap is a little narrower than the ideal, and its indirect gap adds unavoidable losses
Silicon cells are measured at a higher temperature than the limit assumes
The 33 % only applies to stacks of two or more cells
Silicon's gap is wider than the ideal, so it misses more photons
questions.explain: The single-junction optimum is a gap near 1.34 eV; silicon's 1.12 eV is a bit narrower, and as an indirect-gap material it has extra losses, such as Auger recombination, that the Shockley–Queisser model leaves out. A gap wider than the ideal would be the opposite problem.

questions.prompt: Why is an ordinary silicon module on a roof less efficient than the record silicon cell?
choices: Modules are rated under weaker light than 1000 W/m²
Record cells are measured under concentrated sunlight
Roof modules are rated at a higher temperature than lab cells
A record cell is small and carefully made; a module adds gaps, wiring and a frame that make no power
questions.explain: A record is a best case: a small, carefully made cell measured once. A module joins dozens of full-size cells behind glass, and the gaps, wiring and frame take up area without making power. Both are rated under the same standard test conditions, so the light is not the difference.

questions.prompt: A 1 cm² research cell under standard test conditions (1000 W/m²) delivers 27 mW. What is its efficiency?
questions.explain: 1 cm² is 0.0001 m², so the cell receives 1000 × 0.0001 = 0.1 W of light, and 0.027 ÷ 0.1 = 27 %. Treating 1 cm² as 0.01 m² gives 0.27 %, and leaving the area in cm² gives 0.0027 %: convert the area to m² before using W/m².
